obligations.statement: Remote QP certification/confirmation is carried out fully in line with EU legislation and EU GMP guidelines.
obligations.quote: It is a prerequisite that the QP certification/confirmation is carried out in full accordance with EU legislation and EU GMP guidelines

obligations.statement: In all cases the QP performs certification/confirmation from within the EU/EEA (or Northern Ireland), and the location is demonstrated by technical means.
obligations.quote: QP certification / confirmation should take place within the EU/EEA (or Northern Ireland) in all cases. This should be demonstrated by technical means.

obligations.statement: QPs keep their knowledge of the products, manufacturing processes and pharmaceutical quality system up to date.
obligations.quote: QPs are obliged to maintain their knowledge in relation to the products, manufacturing processes and pharmaceutical quality system.

obligations.statement: QPs satisfy themselves that their continuing reliance on the relevant pharmaceutical quality system is well founded.
obligations.quote: QPs also need to be satisfied that their ongoing reliance on the relevant pharmaceutical quality system is well founded.

obligations.statement: The QP can show the competent authority that they know the products and manufacturing processes they are responsible for.
obligations.quote: The QP must be able to demonstrate to the competent authority knowledge of the product and the manufacturing processes for which they are responsible.

obligations.statement: The QP's demonstrated product and process knowledge includes time physically spent on site, as applicable.
obligations.quote: This should include time spent physically on-site as applicable.

obligations.statement: Where remote QP certification/confirmation is used routinely, it is described and controlled within the pharmaceutical quality system.
obligations.quote: Where remote QP certification / confirmation is employed on a routine basis, it must be described and controlled within the pharmaceutical quality system

obligations.statement: Where remote QP certification/confirmation is used routinely, detailed site procedures covering it are in place.
obligations.quote: relevant detailed site procedures should be in place

obligations.statement: In Member States that permit contract QPs, the technical agreement between the MIA holder and the contract QP covers remote certification/confirmation and states when the QP has to attend the site.
obligations.quote: In Member States where use of contract QPs (i.e. a person who is not an employee of the manufacturer but conducting QP activities under the manufacturer’s authorisation) is permitted, the technical agreement between the MIA holder and the QP should also mention remote certification / confirmation, and specify the circumstances under which the QP must attend the site.

obligations.statement: The QP has access to all data and computer system applications needed under Annex 16 to decide on batch certification/confirmation.
obligations.quote: The QP should have access to all information (data and computer system applications) which are necessary according to Annex 16 to make a decision on batch certification / confirmation.

obligations.statement: The MIA holder provides the facilities, equipment and support QPs need to work remotely, including electronic batch certification/confirmation and remote completion of the batch certification register.
obligations.quote: The MIA holder should provide the required facilities to enable QPs to carry out their functions remotely. This includes the equipment and support required to enable electronic batch certification / confirmation and completion of the batch certification register remotely.

obligations.statement: IT systems used for remote batch release meet EU GMP Annex 11 requirements.
obligations.quote: IT systems used for remote batch release should comply with requirements of EU GMP Annex 11.

obligations.statement: Every electronic action the QP takes at the remote location is available at the same time for competent authority inspection at the authorised batch release site.
obligations.quote: All actions carried out by the QP electronically at the remote location should be contemporaneously available for inspection by the competent authorities at the authorised batch release site.

obligations.statement: The MIA holder guarantees that only the QP has editing access to the batch certification function.
obligations.quote: It is the responsibility of the MIA holder to guarantee that a) only the QP has editing access to the batch certification function

obligations.statement: The MIA holder guarantees that data transferred for remote certification are complete and unchanged.
obligations.quote: that data being transferred are complete and unchanged

obligations.statement: The MIA holder guarantees that an electronic signature meeting Annex 11 requirements is in place.
obligations.quote: an electronic signature, reflecting requirements in annex 11, is in place

obligations.statement: QPs can show they are fulfilling their wider duties under Annex 16.
obligations.quote: QPs must be able to demonstrate that they are fulfilling their wider duties in accordance with Annex 16.

obligations.statement: Compliance with these remote certification conditions is verified, for example through the self-inspection programme at the authorised batch release site.
obligations.quote: Compliance with the above points should be verified e.g. as part of the self-inspection programme at the authorized batch release site.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections review ongoing compliance with the company's data governance policy and procedures to confirm they remain effective.
obligations.quote: Ongoing compliance with the company's data governance policy/procedures should be reviewed during self-inspection, to ensure that they remain effective.

obligations.statement: The data integrity self-inspection may also cover elements of the data lifecycle (Q3-Q9).
obligations.quote: This may also include elements of the Data lifecycle discussed in Q3-Q9.

obligations.statement: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) are not delegated.
obligations.quote: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) should not be delegated.

obligations.statement: The quality unit responsibilities are written down, and include at least the responsibilities listed in this clause.
obligations.quote: These responsibilities should be described in writing

obligations.statement: The quality unit releases or rejects all APIs, and releases or rejects intermediates that will be used outside the manufacturer's control.
obligations.quote: Releasing or rejecting all APIs. Releasing or rejecting intermediates for use outside the control of the manufacturing company

obligations.statement: The quality unit sets up a system for releasing or rejecting raw materials, intermediates, packaging materials and labelling materials.
obligations.quote: Establishing a system to release or reject raw materials, intermediates, packaging and labelling materials

obligations.statement: The quality unit reviews the completed batch production and laboratory control records for critical process steps before an API is released for distribution.
obligations.quote: Reviewing completed batch production and laboratory control records of critical process steps before release of the API for distribution

obligations.statement: The quality unit ensures critical deviations are investigated and resolved.
obligations.quote: Making sure that critical deviations are investigated and resolved

obligations.statement: The quality unit approves all specifications and master production instructions.
obligations.quote: Approving all specifications and master production instructions

obligations.statement: The quality unit approves every procedure that affects the quality of intermediates or APIs.
obligations.quote: Approving all procedures impacting the quality of intermediates or APIs

obligations.statement: The quality unit ensures internal audits (self-inspections) are carried out.
obligations.quote: Making sure that internal audits (self-inspections) are performed

obligations.statement: The quality unit approves contract manufacturers of intermediates and APIs.
obligations.quote: Approving intermediate and API contract manufacturers

obligations.statement: The quality unit approves changes that could affect intermediate or API quality.
obligations.quote: Approving changes that potentially impact intermediate or API quality

obligations.statement: The quality unit reviews and approves validation protocols and validation reports.
obligations.quote: Reviewing and approving validation protocols and reports

obligations.statement: The quality unit ensures quality-related complaints are investigated and resolved.
obligations.quote: Making sure that quality related complaints are investigated and resolved

obligations.statement: The quality unit ensures effective systems are in use for maintenance and calibration of critical equipment.
obligations.quote: Making sure that effective systems are used for maintaining and calibrating critical equipment

obligations.statement: The quality unit ensures materials are tested appropriately and the results are reported.
obligations.quote: Making sure that materials are appropriately tested and the results are reported

obligations.statement: The quality unit ensures, where appropriate, that stability data exist to support the retest or expiry dates and storage conditions of APIs and/or intermediates.
obligations.quote: Making sure that there is stability data to support retest or expiry dates and storage conditions on APIs and/or intermediates where appropriate

obligations.statement: The quality unit performs product quality reviews as defined in Section 2.5.
obligations.quote: Performing product quality reviews (as defined in Section 2.5)

obligations.statement: Regular internal audits are carried out to an approved schedule to verify compliance with GMP principles for APIs.
obligations.quote: In order to verify compliance with the principles of GMP for APIs, regular internal audits should be performed in accordance with an approved schedule.

obligations.statement: Audit findings and corrective actions are documented and reported to the firm's responsible management.
obligations.quote: Audit findings and corrective actions should be documented and brought to the attention of responsible management of the firm.

obligations.statement: Agreed corrective actions are completed in a timely and effective way.
obligations.quote: Agreed corrective actions should be completed in a timely and effective manner.

obligations.statement: The distributor carries out and records self-inspections to monitor implementation of, and compliance with, the GDP guidelines.
obligations.quote: The distributor should conduct and record self-inspections in order to monitor the implementation of and com­ pliance with these guidelines.

obligations.statement: Regular self-inspections are performed according to an approved schedule.
obligations.quote: Regular self-inspections should be performed in accordance with an approved schedule.

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether an effective pharmaceutical quality system has been established and implemented.
obligations.quote: establishment and implementation of an effective pharmaceutical quality system

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there are enough competent, suitably qualified personnel.
obligations.quote: sufficient competent and appropriately qualified personnel

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether managerial and supervisory staff for manufacturing and quality activities have defined job descriptions.
obligations.quote: defined job descriptions for managerial and supervisory staff responsible for manufacturing and quality activities

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there are training programmes for all manufacturing and quality staff.
obligations.quote: training programmes for all staff involved in manufacturing and quality activities

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there are health, hygiene and clothing training programmes where needed for the intended operations.
obligations.quote: training programmes related to health, hygiene and clothing as identified as necessary to the intended operations

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether premises and equipment suitable for the intended operations are provided and maintained.
obligations.quote: provision and maintenance of premises and equipment appropriate to the intended operations

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether documentation systems cover all processes and specifications for manufacturing and quality operations.
obligations.quote: documentation system(s) covering all processes and specifications for the various manufacturing and quality operations

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether starting materials, intermediates and excipients are coded and identified so they are fully traceable.
obligations.quote: systems for coding and identifying starting materials, intermediates and excipients to allow full traceability

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there is a supplier qualification programme.
obligations.quote: qualification program of suppliers

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there is a quality control system for the excipient and a responsible person, independent of production, who releases batches.
obligations.quote: system for quality control of the excipient and a responsible person independent from production to release the batches

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether records of incoming materials and excipients, and excipient samples, are retained for the periods required by EudraLex Volume 4, Part II.
obligations.quote: retention of records for incoming materials and excipients and retention of samples of excipients for the peri­ ods required by EudraLex Volume 4, Part II

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there are systems ensuring every outsourced activity is covered by a written contract.
obligations.quote: systems to ensure that any activity contracted out is subject to a written contract

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether an effective system is maintained for reviewing complaints and recalling excipients.
obligations.quote: maintenance of an effective system whereby complaints are reviewed and excipients may be recalled

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there is a change management and deviation management system.
obligations.quote: change management and deviation management system

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there is a self-inspection programme.
obligations.quote: self-inspection program

obligations.statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether environmental control and storage conditions are in place.
obligations.quote: environmental control and storage conditions

obligations.statement: Self-inspections are carried out to monitor implementation of and compliance with GMP principles and to propose any corrective measures needed.
obligations.quote: Self inspections should be conducted in order to monitor the implementation and compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice principles and to propose necessary corrective measures.

obligations.statement: Personnel, premises, equipment, documentation, production, quality control, distribution, complaint and recall arrangements, and self-inspection itself are examined at intervals under a pre-arranged programme to verify conformity with Quality Assurance principles.
obligations.quote: Personnel matters, premises, equipment, documentation, production, quality control, distribution of the medicinal products, arrangements for dealing with complaints and recalls, and self inspection, should be examined at intervals following a pre-arranged programme in order to verify their conformity with the principles of Quality Assurance.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections are carried out independently and in detail by designated competent company staff.
obligations.quote: Self inspections should be conducted in an independent and detailed way by designated competent person(s) from the company.

obligations.statement: Independent audits by external experts may also be used.
obligations.quote: Independent audits by external experts may also be useful.

obligations.statement: Every self-inspection is recorded.
obligations.quote: All self inspections should be recorded.

obligations.statement: Self-inspection reports include all observations and, where applicable, proposed corrective measures.
obligations.quote: Reports should contain all the observations made during the inspections and, where applicable, proposals for corrective measures.

obligations.statement: The actions taken after the self-inspection are recorded.
obligations.quote: Statements on the actions subsequently taken should also be recorded.

obligations.statement: Manufacturers of human medicinal products take into account the GMP guidelines referred to in Article 47, second paragraph, of Directive 2001/83/EC to apply GMP principles consistently.
obligations.quote: In order to ensure the consistent application of the principles of good manufacturing practice, manufacturers of medicinal products for human use and inspectors should consider the guidelines referred to in the second paragraph of Article 47 of Directive 2001/83/EC.

obligations.statement: For advanced therapy medicinal products, the guideline referred to in Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 1394/2007 is applied.
obligations.quote: However, for advanced therapy medicinal products, the guideline referred in Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 1394/2007 (1) should be applied.

obligations.statement: The manufacturer carries out repeated self-inspections within the pharmaceutical quality system to monitor GMP implementation and compliance and to propose any corrective and/or preventive actions needed.
obligations.quote: The manufacturer shall be required to conduct repeated self-inspections as part of the pharmaceutical quality system in order to monitor the implementation and respect of good manufacturing practice and to propose any necessary corrective measures and/or preventive actions.

obligations.statement: Records are kept of self-inspections and of any corrective actions taken afterwards.
obligations.quote: Records shall be maintained of such self-inspections and any corrective actions subsequently taken.

obligations.statement: The manufacturer carries out regular internal audits.
obligations.quote: The manufacturer shall conduct regular internal audits

obligations.statement: The manufacturer follows up on internal audit findings.
obligations.quote: follow-up on the findings

obligations.statement: The quality system is designed, planned, implemented, maintained and continuously improved so that products with the right quality attributes are delivered consistently.
obligations.quote: Product realisation is achieved by designing, planning, implementing, maintaining and continuously improving a system that allows the consistent delivery of products with appropriate quality attributes

obligations.statement: Product and process knowledge is managed across every lifecycle stage.
obligations.quote: Product and process knowledge is managed throughout all lifecycle stages

obligations.statement: Product design and development take GMP requirements into account.
obligations.quote: Medicinal products are designed and developed in a way that takes account of the requirements of Good Manufacturing Practice

obligations.statement: Production and control operations are clearly defined and GMP is adopted.
obligations.quote: Production and control operations are clearly specified and Good Manufacturing Practice adopted

obligations.statement: Management responsibilities are clearly defined.
obligations.quote: Managerial responsibilities are clearly specified

obligations.statement: Arrangements exist for making, supplying and using the correct starting and packaging materials, for selecting and monitoring suppliers, and for checking each delivery comes from the approved supply chain.
obligations.quote: Arrangements are made for the manufacture, supply and use of the correct starting and packaging materials, the selection and monitoring of suppliers and for verifying that each delivery is from the approved supply chain

obligations.statement: Processes are in place to manage outsourced activities.
obligations.quote: Processes are in place to assure the management of outsourced activities

obligations.statement: A state of control is set up and kept through effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality.
obligations.quote: A state of control is established and maintained by developing and using effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality

obligations.statement: Product and process monitoring results are used in batch release, in deviation investigations and for preventive action against future deviations.
obligations.quote: The results of product and processes monitoring are taken into account in batch release, in the investigation of deviations, and, with a view to taking preventive action to avoid potential deviations occurring in the future

obligations.statement: All necessary controls on intermediate products, other in-process controls and validations are performed.
obligations.quote: All necessary controls on intermediate products, and any other in-process controls and validations are carried out

obligations.statement: Continual improvement is supported by quality improvements suited to current process and product knowledge.
obligations.quote: Continual improvement is facilitated through the implementation of quality improvements appropriate to the current level of process and product knowledge

obligations.statement: Planned changes are evaluated in advance and approved before implementation, taking regulatory notification and approval into account where required.
obligations.quote: Arrangements are in place for the prospective evaluation of planned changes and their approval prior to implementation taking into account regulatory notification and approval where required

obligations.statement: After any change is implemented, it is evaluated to confirm the quality objectives were met and product quality was not harmed unintentionally.
obligations.quote: After implementation of any change, an evaluation is undertaken to confirm the quality objectives were achieved and that there was no unintended deleterious impact on product quality

obligations.statement: Investigations of deviations, suspected product defects and other problems use an appropriate level of root cause analysis.
obligations.quote: An appropriate level of root cause analysis should be applied during the investigation of deviations, suspected product defects and other problems.

obligations.statement: Where the true root cause cannot be found, the most likely root cause(s) are considered, identified and addressed.
obligations.quote: In cases where the true root cause(s) of the issue cannot be determined, consideration should be given to identifying the most likely root cause(s) and to addressing those.

obligations.statement: Where human error is suspected or identified as the cause, this is justified after checking that process, procedural or system-based errors have not been overlooked.
obligations.quote: Where human error is suspected or identified as the cause, this should be justified having taken care to ensure that process, procedural or system- based errors or problems have not been overlooked, if present.

obligations.statement: Suitable corrective and/or preventive actions (CAPAs) are identified and implemented following investigations.
obligations.quote: Appropriate corrective actions and/or preventative actions (CAPAs) should be identified and taken in response to investigations.

obligations.statement: CAPA effectiveness is monitored and assessed in line with quality risk management principles.
obligations.quote: The effectiveness of such actions should be monitored and assessed, in line with Quality Risk Management principles.

obligations.statement: No medicinal product is sold or supplied until a Qualified Person has certified that each batch was produced and controlled in line with the Marketing Authorisation and other applicable production, control and release regulations.
obligations.quote: Medicinal products are not sold or supplied before a Qualified Person has certified that each production batch has been produced and controlled in accordance with the requirements of the Marketing Authorisation and any other regulations relevant to the production, control and release of medicinal products

obligations.statement: Arrangements are in place so that, as far as possible, storage, distribution and later handling maintain product quality throughout shelf life.
obligations.quote: Satisfactory arrangements exist to ensure, as far as possible, that the medicinal products are stored, distributed and subsequently handled so that quality is maintained throughout their shelf life

obligations.statement: A self-inspection and/or quality audit process regularly appraises the effectiveness and applicability of the pharmaceutical quality system.
obligations.quote: There is a process for self-inspection and/or quality audit, which regularly appraises the effectiveness and applicability of the Pharmaceutical Quality System.

obligations.statement: The manufacturer, and the marketing authorisation holder where different, evaluate the product quality review results and assess whether corrective and preventive action or revalidation is needed under the pharmaceutical quality system.
obligations.quote: The manufacturer and, where different, marketing authorisation holder should evaluate the results of the review and an assessment made as to whether corrective and preventive action or any revalidation should be undertaken, under the Pharmaceutical Quality System.

obligations.statement: Management procedures exist for the ongoing management and review of these actions.
obligations.quote: There should be management procedures for the ongoing management and review of these actions

obligations.statement: The effectiveness of these management procedures is verified during self-inspection.
obligations.quote: the effectiveness of these procedures verified during self-inspection

obligations.statement: Where scientifically justified, quality reviews may be grouped by product type, such as solid, liquid or sterile dosage forms.
obligations.quote: Quality reviews may be grouped by product type, e.g. solid dosage forms, liquid dosage forms, sterile products, etc. where scientifically justified.

obligations.statement: Where the marketing authorisation holder is not the manufacturer, a technical agreement defines each party's responsibilities for producing the product quality review.
obligations.quote: Where the marketing authorisation holder is not the manufacturer, there should be a technical agreement in place between the various parties that defines their respective responsibilities in producing the product quality review.

obligations.statement: If a report comes from a routine audit verifying that the quality system works as intended, the firm may discard it once all corrections have been verified.
obligations.quote: If the report in question was from a routine audit to verify that the firm's quality system is operating as intended, then it would be acceptable if the firm elected to discard the report once all corrections have been verified.

obligations.statement: Documentation of corrective actions resulting from an internal audit is retained (21 CFR 211.180 and 211.188).
obligations.quote: However, any documentation of corrective action as a result of such an audit would have to be retained (see §§ 211.180 and 211.188).

obligations.statement: If an internal audit leads to a process change (for example a new mixing time), all affected procedures, including the master production record, are updated to reflect it.
obligations.quote: if a routine internal audit finds a problem with a mixing step and the outcome is a change in mixing time, all affected procedures, including the master production record, are to reflect the necessary changes

obligations.statement: Any investigation of the problem's impact on related batches is retained and made available for FDA inspection (21 CFR 211.192).
obligations.quote: Any investigation into the impact this problem had on related batches is to be retained and also made available for inspection by FDA (see § 211.192).

obligations.statement: Reports of investigations or evaluations for complaints, vendor qualification, periodic record and data review, and failure investigations are open to FDA inspection and kept for at least the period set in the CGMP regulations (21 CFR 211.180).
obligations.quote: Such records are subject to FDA inspection and must be retained for at least the time specified in the CGMP regulations (see § 211.180).

obligations.statement: The quality unit section of the quality agreement sets out in detail how the parties will work together so products are made in CGMP compliance.
obligations.quote: The section of a quality agreement that addresses each party’s quality unit activities should define in detail how the parties will work together to ensure that products are manufactured in compliance with CGMP.

obligations.statement: The quality unit section of the quality agreement is clear about product release.
obligations.quote: In particular, this section of the quality agreement should be clear with respect to product release.

obligations.statement: The contract facility approves or rejects the products or results of its own manufacturing operations, such as test results, finished dosage forms or in-process materials.
obligations.quote: Contract facilities are responsible for approving or rejecting the product or results of their manufacturing operations (e.g., test results, finished dosage forms, or in-process materials).

obligations.statement: The owner approves or rejects drugs made by the contract facility, including final release.
obligations.quote: owners are responsible for approving or rejecting drugs manufactured by the contract facility, 23 including for final release.

obligations.statement: The owner never introduces, delivers, or causes the introduction or delivery of, adulterated or misbranded drugs into interstate commerce.
obligations.quote: In all cases, the owner must not introduce or deliver into interstate commerce, or cause to be introduced or delivered into interstate commerce, any drugs that are adulterated or misbranded.

obligations.statement: The quality agreement describes how and when owner and contract facility communicate, verbally and in writing, and names the contact people in each organisation.
obligations.quote: Within its quality unit activities, a quality agreement should describe how and when the owner and contract facility will communicate with each other, both verbally and in writing. This includes identifying appropriate contact personnel within the owner’s and contract facility’s organization.

obligations.statement: The quality agreement covers audits, inspections and communication of findings.
obligations.quote: Quality agreements should also cover audits, inspections, and communication of findings.

obligations.statement: The quality agreement lets the owner evaluate and audit the contract facility for CGMP compliance of specific operations, covering both routine and for-cause audits.
obligations.quote: The agreement should allow owners to evaluate and audit contract facilities to ensure CGMP compliance for specific operations. This provision should cover both routine quality audits and for-cause audits.

obligations.statement: The quality agreement sets the owner's and contract facility's expectations for FDA pre-approval, routine surveillance and for-cause inspections, considering the products or services involved.
obligations.quote: The agreement should also set owner and contract facility expectations regarding FDA inspections (pre-approval, routine surveillance, and for-cause) with consideration for the nature of the products to be manufactured and/or services to be provided.

obligations.statement: The quality agreement includes the agreed arrangements for communicating inspection observations and findings and relevant FDA actions and correspondence.
obligations.quote: It should include the parties’ agreed-upon provisions for communicating inspection observations and findings, as well as relevant FDA actions and correspondence.

obligations.statement: The quality agreement states when, how and what the contractor will report to the owner about objectionable conditions found during inspections and audits of the contract facility.
obligations.quote: Because contract facilities often provide services to multiple owners, the quality agreement should address when, how, and what information the contractor will report to owners about objectionable conditions observed during inspections and audits of the contract facility.

obligations.statement: Trends are monitored continually and systems are improved.
obligations.quote: Quality systems call for continually monitoring trends and improving systems.

obligations.statement: Quality system procedures collect data from monitoring, measurement, complaint handling and other activities and track it over time, as appropriate.
obligations.quote: Quality systems procedures involve collecting data from monitoring, measurement, complaint handling, or other activities, and tracking this data over time, as appropriate.

obligations.statement: Product review is carried out at least annually as required by 21 CFR 211.180(e).
obligations.quote: the CGMP regulations (§ 211.180(e)) require product review on at least an annual basis

obligations.statement: Data are trended more often than annually, at a frequency set by risk.
obligations.quote: a quality systems approach calls for trending on a more frequent basis as determined by risk

obligations.statement: Audits are carried out at planned intervals to evaluate whether the quality system is effectively implemented and maintained and whether processes and products meet established parameters and specifications.
obligations.quote: A quality systems approach calls for audits to be conducted at planned intervals to evaluate effective implementation and maintenance of the quality system and to determine if processes and products meet established parameters and specifications.

obligations.statement: Documented audit procedures ensure the audit schedule accounts for the relative risk of quality system activities, previous audit results and corrective actions, and the need to cover the whole system.
obligations.quote: audit procedures should be developed and documented to ensure that the planned audit schedule takes into account the relative risks of the various quality system activities, the results of previous audits and corrective actions, and the need to audit the complete system.

obligations.statement: Procedures describe how auditors are trained in gathering objective evidence, their responsibilities and audit procedures.
obligations.quote: Procedures should describe how auditors are trained in objective evidence gathering, their responsibilities, and auditing procedures.

obligations.statement: Procedures define audit activities, including scope and methodology, auditor selection and audit conduct (plans, opening meetings, interviews, closing meeting and reports).
obligations.quote: Procedures should also define auditing activities such as the scope and methodology of the audit, selection of auditors, and audit conduct (audit plans, opening meetings, interviews, closing meeting and reports).

obligations.statement: Records of audit findings are kept and responsibility for follow-up is assigned to prevent recurrence.
obligations.quote: It is critical to maintain records of audit findings and assign responsibility for follow-up to prevent problems from recurring

obligations.statement: Managers of audited areas act promptly to resolve audit findings and ensure follow-up actions are completed, verified and recorded.
obligations.quote: The quality systems model calls for managers who are responsible for the areas audited to take timely action to resolve audit findings and ensure that follow-up actions are completed, verified, and recorded.

obligations.statement: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) are not delegated.
obligations.quote: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) should not be delegated.

obligations.statement: The quality unit responsibilities are written down, and include at least the responsibilities listed in this clause.
obligations.quote: These responsibilities should be described in writing

obligations.statement: The quality unit releases or rejects all APIs, and releases or rejects intermediates that will be used outside the manufacturer's control.
obligations.quote: Releasing or rejecting all APIs. Releasing or rejecting intermediates for use outside the control of the manufacturing company

obligations.statement: The quality unit sets up a system for releasing or rejecting raw materials, intermediates, packaging materials and labelling materials.
obligations.quote: Establishing a system to release or reject raw materials, intermediates, packaging and labelling materials

obligations.statement: The quality unit reviews the completed batch production and laboratory control records for critical process steps before an API is released for distribution.
obligations.quote: Reviewing completed batch production and laboratory control records of critical process steps before release of the API for distribution

obligations.statement: The quality unit ensures critical deviations are investigated and resolved.
obligations.quote: Making sure that critical deviations are investigated and resolved

obligations.statement: The quality unit approves all specifications and master production instructions.
obligations.quote: Approving all specifications and master production instructions

obligations.statement: The quality unit approves every procedure that affects the quality of intermediates or APIs.
obligations.quote: Approving all procedures impacting the quality of intermediates or APIs

obligations.statement: The quality unit ensures internal audits (self-inspections) are carried out.
obligations.quote: Making sure that internal audits (self-inspections) are performed

obligations.statement: The quality unit approves contract manufacturers of intermediates and APIs.
obligations.quote: Approving intermediate and API contract manufacturers

obligations.statement: The quality unit approves changes that could affect intermediate or API quality.
obligations.quote: Approving changes that potentially impact intermediate or API quality

obligations.statement: The quality unit reviews and approves validation protocols and validation reports.
obligations.quote: Reviewing and approving validation protocols and reports

obligations.statement: The quality unit ensures quality-related complaints are investigated and resolved.
obligations.quote: Making sure that quality related complaints are investigated and resolved

obligations.statement: The quality unit ensures effective systems are in use for maintenance and calibration of critical equipment.
obligations.quote: Making sure that effective systems are used for maintaining and calibrating critical equipment

obligations.statement: The quality unit ensures materials are tested appropriately and the results are reported.
obligations.quote: Making sure that materials are appropriately tested and the results are reported

obligations.statement: The quality unit ensures, where appropriate, that stability data exist to support the retest or expiry dates and storage conditions of APIs and/or intermediates.
obligations.quote: Making sure that there is stability data to support retest or expiry dates and storage conditions on APIs and/or intermediates where appropriate

obligations.statement: The quality unit performs product quality reviews as defined in Section 2.5.
obligations.quote: Performing product quality reviews (as defined in Section 2.5)

obligations.statement: A mechanism exists at the site, such as a quality manual, documentation, flowcharts or procedures, that shows management, staff and inspectors in an easily understood way how the PQS works across the product lifecycle.
obligations.quote: A mechanism should be established to demonstrate at a site how the PQS operates across the product lifecycle, in an easily understandable way for management, staff and regulatory inspectors, e.g., a quality manual, documentation, flowcharts, procedures.

obligations.statement: The company may run an internal audit programme that routinely audits the PQS to confirm it functions at a high level.
obligations.quote: Companies can implement a program in which the PQS is routinely audited in-house (i.e., internal audit program) to ensure that the system is functioning at a high level.

obligations.statement: As a licence condition, the manufacturer complies with the GMP requirements of Schedule M.
obligations.quote: The manufacturer is required to comply with the requirements of Good Manufacturing Practices prescribed in Schedule M under the conditions of the licence so as to ensure that the drugs manufacturers in the country conform to the standards prescribed for them.

obligations.statement: If a distributor's or agent's activity is subcontracted, the subcontractor is appropriately authorised for that activity and meets the same standards as the distributor.
obligations.quote: If the activity of a distributor or his or her agent is subcontracted to another entity, the person or entity to which the activity is subcontracted shall be appropriately authorized to perform the subcontracted activity and shall uphold the same standards as the distributor.

obligations.statement: Distributor and retailer activities are supervised by qualified staff as specified in the Drugs Rules 1945.
obligations.quote: The activity of distributor and retailer shall be taken under supervision of qualified staff as specified in Drugs Rules 1945.

obligations.statement: Entities storing and distributing pharmaceutical products have a comprehensively designed, documented and correctly implemented quality system covering GSP, GDP, quality risk management and management review.
obligations.quote: Entities involved in the storage and distribution of pharmaceutical products should shall have a comprehensively designed, documented and correctly implemented quality system that incorporates GSP, GDP, principles of quality risk management and management review.

obligations.statement: Senior management ensures an effective quality system is established, resourced, implemented and maintained.
obligations.quote: Senior management has the ultimate responsibility to ensure that an effective quality system is established, resourced, implemented and maintained.

obligations.statement: The distribution quality system ensures that GSP and GDP are adopted and implemented so product quality is maintained through the supply chain for the whole shelf life, and products are properly procured, stored, distributed and delivered to the right recipients.
obligations.quote: GSP and GDP are adopted and implemented to ensure that the quality of pharmaceutical products is maintained throughout their shelf life in the supply chain; and pharmaceutical products are appropriately procured, stored, distributed and delivered to the appropriate recipients

obligations.statement: The distribution quality system ensures that operations are clearly set out in written procedures.
obligations.quote: operations are clearly specified in written procedures

obligations.statement: The distribution quality system ensures that responsibilities are clearly set out in job descriptions.
obligations.quote: responsibilities are clearly specified in job descriptions

obligations.statement: The distribution quality system ensures that all risks are identified and necessary, effective controls are implemented.
obligations.quote: all risks are identified and necessary, effective controls are implemented

obligations.statement: The distribution quality system ensures that processes exist to manage outsourced activities.
obligations.quote: processes are in place to assure the management of outsourced activities

obligations.statement: The distribution quality system ensures that a procedure for self-inspection and quality audits exists.
obligations.quote: there is a procedure for self-inspection and quality audits

obligations.statement: The distribution quality system ensures that a quality risk management system exists.
obligations.quote: there is a system for quality risk management

obligations.statement: The distribution quality system ensures that systems exist for managing returns, complaints and recalls.
obligations.quote: there are systems for managing returns, complaints and recalls

obligations.statement: The distribution quality system ensures that systems exist for managing changes, deviations and CAPAs.
obligations.quote: there are systems to manage changes, deviations and corrective an preventive actions (CAPAs)

obligations.statement: An authorised, written quality policy states the overall quality intentions and requirements.
obligations.quote: There shall be an authorized, written quality policy describing the overall intentions and requirements regarding quality.

obligations.statement: The quality policy may be reflected in a quality manual.
obligations.quote: This may be reflected in a quality manual.

obligations.statement: An appropriate organisational structure exists and is shown in an authorised organisation chart.
obligations.quote: There shall be an appropriate organizational structure. This shall be presented in an authorized organizational chart.

obligations.statement: Personnel responsibilities, authority and interrelationships are clearly shown.
obligations.quote: The responsibility, authority and interrelationships of personnel shall be clearly indicated.

obligations.statement: Contract acceptors are audited periodically.
obligations.quote: There shall be periodic audit of contract acceptors.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections are part of the quality system.
obligations.quote: Self-inspections shall be included in the quality system.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections are carried out to monitor implementation of and compliance with GDP principles and, where needed, to trigger corrective and preventive measures.
obligations.quote: These shall be conducted to monitor implementation and compliance with the principles of GDP and, if necessary, to trigger corrective and preventive measures.

obligations.statement: A designated, competent person carries out self-inspection independently and in detail.
obligations.quote: A designated, competent person shall conduct self-inspection in an independent and detailed way.

obligations.statement: Self-inspection results are recorded, including all observations and, where required, proposed corrective measures.
obligations.quote: There shall be records of self-inspection results which shall contain all observations made during the inspection and if required proposal for corrective measures.

obligations.statement: An effective follow-up programme exists, and management evaluates the inspection report and the corrective actions taken.
obligations.quote: There shall be an effective follow-up programme and evaluation of inspection report and corrective action taken by the management.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections are carried out periodically to an annual schedule.
obligations.quote: Self-inspections should be conducted periodically, according to an annual schedule.

obligations.statement: The self-inspection team is free from bias.
obligations.quote: The team conducting the inspection should be free from bias

obligations.statement: Each self-inspection team member has appropriate knowledge and experience.
obligations.quote: individual members should have appropriate knowledge and experience

answer.no_obligation_reason: The clause defines how the date of manufacture is determined for the monographs in this Part by reference to Rule 109; it is a definition, not an obligation on a site.

obligations.statement: The quality system is designed, qualified, planned, implemented, maintained and continuously improved so products with the right quality attributes are delivered consistently.
obligations.quote: product realisation is achieved by designing, qualifying, planning, implementing, maintaining and continuously improving a system that allows the consistent delivery of products with appropriate quality attributes

obligations.statement: Product and process knowledge is managed across every lifecycle stage.
obligations.quote: product and process knowledge is managed throughout all lifecycle stages

obligations.statement: Product design and development take into account GMP and other GxP requirements such as GLP and GCP.
obligations.quote: pharmaceutical products are designed and developed in a way that takes into account, the requirements of GMP and other GXPs such as those of Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) and Good Clinical Practices (GCP)

obligations.statement: Production and QC operations are clearly specified in writing and GMP requirements are adopted.
obligations.quote: production and quality control operations shall be clearly specified in a written form and GMP requirements are adopted

obligations.statement: Management responsibilities are clearly set out in job descriptions.
obligations.quote: managerial responsibilities are clearly specified in the job descriptions

obligations.statement: Arrangements exist for making, supplying and using the correct starting and packaging materials, for selecting and monitoring suppliers, and for checking each delivery is the correct material from the approved supply chain.
obligations.quote: arrangements are made for the manufacture, supply and use of the correct starting and packaging materials, the selection and monitoring of suppliers and for verifying that each delivery is the correct material from the approved supply chain

obligations.statement: All necessary controls on starting materials, intermediates and bulk products, other in-process controls, calibrations and validations are performed.
obligations.quote: all necessary controls on starting materials, intermediate products, and bulk products and other in-process controls, calibrations and validations are carried out

obligations.statement: The finished product is correctly processed and checked to defined procedures.
obligations.quote: the finished product is correctly processed and checked, according to the defined procedures

obligations.statement: No product is sold or supplied until the authorised persons have certified that each batch was produced and controlled in line with the licence and other applicable production, control and release regulations.
obligations.quote: pharmaceutical products are not sold or supplied before the authorised persons have certified that each production batch has been produced and controlled in accordance with the requirements of the licence and other applicable regulations relevant to the production, control and release of pharmaceutical products

obligations.statement: Processes are in place to manage outsourced activities.
obligations.quote: processes are in place to ensure the management of outsourced activities

obligations.statement: Arrangements are in place so that, as far as possible, storage, distribution and later handling maintain product quality throughout shelf life.
obligations.quote: satisfactory arrangements exist to ensure, as far as possible, that the pharmaceutical products are stored, distributed and subsequently handled so that quality is maintained throughout their shelf-life

obligations.statement: A self-inspection or quality audit procedure regularly appraises the effectiveness and applicability of the product quality system.
obligations.quote: there is a procedure for self-inspection or quality audit that regularly appraises the effectiveness and applicability of the product quality system

obligations.statement: Products and processes are monitored and the results are used in batch release, deviation investigations and preventive action against future deviations.
obligations.quote: product and processes are monitored and the results taken into account in batch release, in the investigation of deviations and, with a view to taking preventive action to avoid potential deviations occurring in the future

obligations.statement: Planned changes are evaluated and approved in advance, before implementation, taking regulatory notification and approval into account where required.
obligations.quote: arrangements are in place for the prospective evaluation and approval of planned changes and their approval prior to their implementation, taking into account regulatory notification and approval where required

obligations.statement: After any change is implemented, it is evaluated to confirm the quality objectives were met and product quality was not adversely affected unintentionally.
obligations.quote: After implementation of any change, an evaluation is undertaken to confirm that the quality objectives were achieved and that there was no unintended adverse impact on product quality

obligations.statement: Regular product quality reviews are carried out to verify process consistency and identify needed improvements.
obligations.quote: regular reviews of the quality of pharmaceutical products are conducted with the objective of verifying the consistency of the process and identifying where there is a need for improvement

obligations.statement: A state of control is set up and kept through effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality.
obligations.quote: a state of control is established and maintained by developing and using effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality

obligations.statement: Continual improvement is supported by quality improvements suited to current process and product knowledge.
obligations.quote: continual improvement is facilitated through the implementation of quality improvements appropriate to the current level of process and product knowledge

obligations.statement: A quality risk management system is in place.
obligations.quote: there is a system for QRM

obligations.statement: Deviations, suspected product defects and other problems are reported, investigated and recorded.
obligations.quote: deviations, suspected product defects and other problems are reported, investigated and recorded

obligations.statement: These investigations use an appropriate level of root cause analysis.
obligations.quote: An appropriate level of root cause analysis is applied during such investigations.

obligations.statement: The most likely root causes are identified.
obligations.quote: The most likely root causes shall be identified

obligations.statement: Appropriate corrective and preventive actions are identified and implemented.
obligations.quote: appropriate corrective and preventive actions shall be identified and taken

obligations.statement: CAPA effectiveness is monitored.
obligations.quote: The effectiveness of corrective and preventive actions shall be monitored.

obligations.statement: The manufacturer evaluates the quality review results and assesses whether corrective and preventive actions or revalidation are needed under the product quality system.
obligations.quote: The manufacturer shall evaluate the results of the review and an assessment shall be made as to whether corrective and preventive actions or any revalidation shall be undertaken, under the product quality system.

obligations.statement: Corrective and preventive actions are completed on time and effectively, following documented procedures.
obligations.quote: Corrective and preventive actions shall be completed in a timely and effective manner, according to documented procedures.

obligations.statement: Procedures exist for the ongoing management and review of these actions.
obligations.quote: There shall be procedures for the on-going management and review of these actions

obligations.statement: The effectiveness of these procedures is verified during self-inspection.
obligations.quote: the effectiveness of these procedures shall be verified during self-inspection

obligations.statement: Where scientifically justified, quality reviews may be grouped by product type, such as solid, liquid or sterile products.
obligations.quote: Quality reviews may be grouped by product type e.g., solid dosage forms, liquid dosage forms, or sterile products, where scientifically justified.

obligations.statement: A technical agreement defines each party's responsibilities for producing the quality review.
obligations.quote: There shall be a technical agreement in place between the various parties that defines their respective responsibilities in producing the quality review.

obligations.statement: The authorised person responsible for final batch certification ensures the quality review is done on time and is accurate.
obligations.quote: The authorised person responsible for final batch certification shall ensure that the quality review is performed in a timely manner and is accurate.

obligations.statement: The contract describes how rejected starting materials, intermediates, bulk and finished products are handled.
obligations.quote: The contract shall describe the handling of starting materials, intermediate, bulk and finished products, if they are rejected.

obligations.statement: The contract describes the procedure to follow if contract analysis shows the tested product has to be rejected.
obligations.quote: It shall also describe the procedure to be followed if the contract analysis shows that the tested product must be rejected.

obligations.statement: The self-inspection programme is designed to find any GMP implementation shortcomings and recommend needed corrective actions.
obligations.quote: The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections are carried out routinely.
obligations.quote: Self-inspections shall be performed routinely

obligations.statement: Additional self-inspections may be carried out on special occasions, such as a product recall, repeated rejections or an announced regulatory inspection.
obligations.quote: may be, in addition, performed on special occasions e.g., in the case of product recall or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the regulatory authorities is announced

obligations.statement: The self-inspection team is made up of people able to assess GMP implementation objectively.
obligations.quote: The team responsible for self-inspection shall consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of good manufacturing practices objectively.

obligations.statement: Every corrective action recommendation is implemented.
obligations.quote: All recommendations for corrective action shall be implemented.

obligations.statement: The self-inspection procedure is documented.
obligations.quote: The procedure for self- inspection shall be documented

obligations.statement: An effective self-inspection follow-up programme exists.
obligations.quote: there shall be an effective follow- up programme

obligations.statement: Written self-inspection instructions are established to give a minimum, uniform standard of requirements.
obligations.quote: Written instructions for self-inspection shall be established to provide a minimum and uniform standard of requirements.

obligations.statement: The self-inspection instructions may include GMP questionnaires covering at least personnel; premises and personnel facilities; building and equipment maintenance; storage of starting materials and finished products; equipment; production and in-process controls; QC; documentation; sanitation and hygiene; validation and revalidation; instrument calibration; recalls; complaints; label control; and previous self-inspection results and corrective steps.
obligations.quote: These may include questionnaires on good manufacturing practices requirements covering at least the following items, namely:- (a) personnel; (b) premises including personnel facilities; (c) maintenance of buildings and equipment; (d) storage of starting materials and finished products; (e) equipment; (f) production and in-process controls; (g) quality control (QC); (h) documentation; (i) sanitation and hygiene; (j) validation and revalidation programmes; (k) calibration of instruments or measurement systems; (l) recall procedures; (m) complaints management; (n) labels control; and (o) results of previous self-inspections and any corrective steps taken.

obligations.statement: Management appoints a self-inspection team of subject experts who are familiar with GMP.
obligations.quote: Management shall appoint a self-inspection team consisting of experts in their respective fields who are familiar with GMP.

obligations.statement: Self-inspection team members may come from inside or outside the company.
obligations.quote: The members of the team may be appointed from inside or outside the company.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections are carried out at a frequency set by company needs, but at least once a year.
obligations.quote: The frequency with which self- inspections are conducted may depend on company requirements but shall be at least once in a year.
numbers: at least once in a year

obligations.statement: The self-inspection frequency is stated in the procedure.
obligations.quote: The frequency shall be stated in the procedure.

obligations.statement: A report is written when each self-inspection is completed.
obligations.quote: A report shall be made at the completion of a self-inspection.

obligations.statement: The self-inspection report contains the results, the evaluation and conclusions, and the recommended corrective actions.
obligations.quote: The report shall include the following, namely:- (a) self-inspection results; (b) evaluation and conclusions; and (c) recommended corrective actions.

obligations.statement: An effective self-inspection follow-up programme exists.
obligations.quote: There shall be an effective follow-up programme.

obligations.statement: Company management evaluates the self-inspection report and the corrective actions, as necessary.
obligations.quote: The company management shall evaluate both the self-inspection report and the corrective actions as necessary.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections may be supplemented by a quality audit.
obligations.quote: It may be useful to supplement self-inspections with a quality audit.

obligations.statement: Quality audits may be extended to suppliers and contractors.
obligations.quote: Such audits may also be extended to suppliers and contractors.

obligations.statement: The person responsible for quality control, together with other relevant departments, approves suppliers able to reliably supply starting and packaging materials that meet specifications.
obligations.quote: The person responsible for quality control shall have responsibility, together with other relevant departments, for approving suppliers who can reliably supply starting and packaging materials that meet established specifications.

obligations.statement: Suppliers are evaluated before being approved and added to the approved suppliers' list or specifications.
obligations.quote: Before suppliers are approved and included in the approved suppliers’ list or specifications, they shall be evaluated.

obligations.statement: The supplier evaluation considers the supplier's history and the nature of the materials supplied.
obligations.quote: The evaluation shall take into account a supplier’s history and the nature of the materials to be supplied.

obligations.statement: If a supplier audit is required, it determines whether the supplier can meet GMP standards.
obligations.quote: If an audit is required, it shall determine the supplier’s ability to conform with good manufacturing practices standards.
